votes.reason: Biotech falls within Healthcare, my top call, which broke out to an all-time high on its own FDA-approval news rather than on this week's PCE, NVDA and Warsh events, and REGN's +27.3% four-week gain shows it is one of the names driving that move.

At about 12% of XLV and a 52-week closing high, LLY is the most direct way to own the Healthcare rotation I called, and the drug-pricing or tariff headlines I named as the pharma risk are something to watch, not something that has happened this week.

An oil producer is the purest way to play my Energy call that the oil premium now rests on a real Hormuz supply cut, and COP fills the hedge role I gave Energy against a jump in the 10Y from a hot PCE or a hawkish Warsh; the call fails only if tankers start moving or Iran talks restart.

Financials is not one of my four sectors, but I made no call against it (only Technology and Real Estate were ruled out), and its role as a hedge against rising yields fits the 10Y risk that my Energy and Staples calls both name, so my lens gives no concrete reason to object.

PEP is one of the names I cited as drawing money within Consumer Staples while WMT fell, and as a low-beta multinational helped by the weak dollar it fits the cushion role I gave Staples, my weakest call, if NVDA disappoints.
